schema_notes: Each company entry is ground truth for eval/run_eval.ts to compare pipeline output against.

Every factual claim below carries a `sources` citation. Nothing here is inferred, estimated, or carried over from AlphaMap's own (possibly wrong) DB rows — that would defeat the point of a golden set.

Where independent sources genuinely disagree (see Fresha.employee_count), the field is left null/range-only rather than picking one number to look complete — this mirrors ground rule 2 (missing is better than wrong) applied to the golden set itself.

funding_rounds[].confidence is 'high' (2+ independent primary/trade-press sources agree), 'medium' (1 primary source, or 2+ aggregators agreeing), or 'low' (single aggregator source only) — used to weight precision scoring, not just hit/miss.
hard_case_tags follow the categories in the v2 spec Section 6 (issue 13): common_name, non_us, rebrand_domain_change, series_a_start, stealth_no_data, went_public.
coverage_status: STARTER SET — 2 of target 50-150+ companies. See the v2 rollout thread for how the remaining entries get added (this session's research vs. team-supplied verification vs. hybrid).

funding_rounds.notes: CEO Ian Cinnamon explicitly described this as the company's THIRD distinct $200M round in ~14 months, deliberately not labeled with a series letter. This and the Series D above are two SEPARATE real events, not a duplicate — see production_bug_notes.

companies.production_bug_notes: AlphaMap's live DB showed 'Growth (Jun 2026)' and 'Series D (Apr 2026)' as two $200M/$2.3B rows and treated them as a duplicate to merge. Verified research shows the REAL Series D was Sept 2025 (not Apr 2026) at a ~$1B valuation, and the Jun 2026 round is a genuinely separate, later, third $200M raise at $2.3B. The production data's 'Apr 2026' date for 'Series D' does not match any real event found — it appears to be a hallucinated/mis-dated entry, not a legitimate duplicate of the June round. The correct fix is 6 distinct rounds with correct dates, not a 2-into-1 merge.

companies.rebrand_notes: Launched 2015 as 'Shedul'; rebranded to 'Fresha' in 2020. A v2 entity/domain check must not treat pre-2020 Shedul-era sources as a different company, and must not let a stale 'shedul.com' domain reference fail domain verification against the current fresha.com.

funding_rounds.notes: Confirmed via General Atlantic's own BusinessWire press release — highest-confidence source in this set.

Reported as a 'Series C Plus' top-up by aggregators only; not confirmed via a primary source. A real test case for round-dedup logic: is this a distinct round, or should it merge with the June 2021 Series C above?

One aggregator labels this 'Series C'; another calls it an unlabeled growth round. Lead investor also appears elsewhere as unspecified. Recorded here as the best-supported version; flagged for round-type ambiguity.

companies.total_raised_discrepancy_notes: Reported aggregate ($285M, Tracxn/Seedtable) does not equal the sum of the rounds we could individually verify ($258.5M) — a real, common gap between 'headline total raised' and an itemized, source-by-source round list. v2's 'never compute Total Raised from a model-returned total' rule (issue 5) should recompute from the rounds actually stored, which will legitimately be LOWER than some press-reported aggregates until every round is itemized.
companies.employee_count_discrepancy_notes: LinkedIn's own self-reported company-size bucket is 201-500, but LinkedIn's 'people' count surfaces ~728, and third-party aggregators report 500 / 718 / 916 depending on collection date through 2026. No single authoritative figure exists. Golden value is deliberately the LinkedIn-bucket RANGE (the closest to a company-declared figure), with employee_count left null rather than picking one aggregator number. The production bug (140,000 employees) is wrong by 2-3 orders of magnitude against EVERY one of these candidates, so it's caught regardless of which is 'true' — this entry is really testing the headcount_outlier validation rule (issue 4), not precision on the exact count.
